types.name: WebOptions
types.description: Contains document-level attributes used by Microsoft Word when you save a document as a webpage or open a webpage.
types.remarks: You can return or set attributes either at the application (global) level or at the document level. (Note that attribute values can be different from one document to another, depending on the attribute value at the time the document was saved.) Document-level attribute settings override application-level attribute settings. Application-level attributes are contained in the DefaultWebOptions object. Use the WebOptions property to return the WebOptions object. The following example checks to see whether PNG (Portable Network Graphics) is allowed as an image format and then sets the strImageFileType variable accordingly.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft Word application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which the specified object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns an Object that represents the parent object of the specified WebOptions object.

properties.name: OptimizeForBrowser
properties.description: True if Word optimizes the specified Web page for the web browser specified by the BrowserLevel property. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: BrowserLevel
properties.description: Returns or sets WdBrowserLevel that represents the level of web browser at which you want to target the specified Web page. Read/write.

properties.name: RelyOnCSS
properties.description: True if cascading style sheets (CSS) are used for font formatting when you view a saved document in a web browser. The default value is True. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: OrganizeInFolder
properties.description: True if all supporting files, such as background textures and graphics, are organized in a separate folder when you save the specified document as a webpage. False if supporting files are saved in the same folder as the webpage. The default value is True. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: UseLongFileNames
properties.description: True if long file names are used when you save the document as a webpage. False if long file names are not used and the DOS file name format (8.3) is used. The default value is True. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: RelyOnVML
properties.description: True if image files are not generated from drawing objects when you save a document as a webpage. False if images are generated. The default value is False. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: AllowPNG
properties.description: True if PNG (Portable Network Graphics) is allowed as an image format when you save a document as a webpage. False if PNG is not allowed as an output format. The default value is False. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: ScreenSize
properties.description: Returns or sets the ideal minimum screen size (width by height, in pixels) that you should use when viewing the saved document in a web browser. Read/write MsoScreenSize.

properties.name: PixelsPerInch
properties.description: Returns or sets the density (pixels per inch) of graphics images and table cells on a webpage. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Encoding
properties.description: Returns or sets the document encoding (code page or character set) to be used by the web browser when you view the saved document. Read/write MsoEncoding.

properties.name: FolderSuffix
properties.description: Returns the folder suffix that Microsoft Word uses when you save a document as a webpage, use long file names, and choose to save supporting files in a separate folder (that is, if the UseLongFileNames and OrganizeInFolder properties are set to True). Read-only String.

properties.name: TargetBrowser
properties.description: Sets or returns an MsoTargetBrowser constant representing the target browser for documents viewed in a web browser. Read/write.

methods.name: UseDefaultFolderSuffix
methods.description: Sets the folder suffix for the specified document to the default suffix for the language support you have selected or installed.

types.name: Window
types.description: Represents a window. Many document characteristics, such as scroll bars and rulers, are actually properties of the window.
types.remarks: The Window object is a member of the Windows collection. The Windows collection for the Application object contains all the windows in the application, whereas the Windows collection for the Document object contains only the windows that display the specified document. Use Windows (Index), where Index is the window name or the index number, to return a single Window object. The following example maximizes the Document1 window. The index number is the number to the left of the window name on the Window menu. The following example displays the caption of the first window in the Windows collection. Use the Add method or the NewWindow method to add a new window to the Windows collection. Each of the following statements creates a new window for the document in the active window. A colon (:) and a number appear in the window caption when more than one window is open for a document. When you switch the view to print preview, a new window is created. This window is removed from the Windows collection when you close print preview.

properties.name: Application
properties.description: Returns an Application object that represents the Microsoft OfficeWord application.

properties.name: Creator
properties.description: Returns a 32-bit integer that indicates the application in which the specified object was created. Read-only Long.

properties.name: Parent
properties.description: Returns an Object that represents the parent object of the specified Window object.

properties.name: ActivePane
properties.description: Returns a Pane object that represents the active pane for the specified window. Read-only.

properties.name: Document
properties.description: Returns a Document object associated with the specified pane, window, or selection. Read-only.

properties.name: Panes
properties.description: Returns a Panes collection that represents all the window panes for the specified window.

properties.name: Selection
properties.description: Returns the Selection object that represents a selected range or the insertion point. Read-only.

properties.name: Left
properties.description: Returns or sets a Long that represents the horizontal position of the specified window, measured in points. Read/write.

properties.name: Top
properties.description: Returns or sets the vertical position of the specified document window, in points. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Width
properties.description: Returns or sets the width of the specified document window, in points. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Height
properties.description: Returns or sets the height of the window (in points). Read/write Long.

properties.name: Split
properties.description: True if the window is split into multiple panes. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: SplitVertical
properties.description: Returns or sets the vertical split percentage for the specified window. Read/write Long.

properties.name: Caption
properties.description: Returns or sets the caption text for the window that is displayed in the title bar of the document or application window. Read/write String.

properties.name: WindowState
properties.description: Returns or sets the state of the specified document window or task window. Read/write WdWindowState.

properties.name: DisplayRulers
properties.description: True if rulers are displayed for the specified window or pane. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: DisplayVerticalRuler
properties.description: True if a vertical ruler is displayed for the specified window or pane. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: View
properties.description: Returns a View object that represents the view for the specified window or pane.

properties.name: Type
properties.description: Returns the window type. Read-only WdWindowType.

properties.name: Next
properties.description: Returns the next document window in the collection of open document windows. Read-only.

properties.name: Previous
properties.description: Returns the previous document window in the collection open document windows. Read-only.

properties.name: DisplayVerticalScrollBar
properties.description: True if a vertical scroll bar is displayed for the specified window. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: DisplayHorizontalScrollBar
properties.description: True if a horizontal scroll bar is displayed for the specified window. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: StyleAreaWidth
properties.description: Returns or sets the width of the style area in points. Read/write Single.

properties.name: DisplayScreenTips
properties.description: True if comments, footnotes, endnotes, and hyperlinks are displayed as tips. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: HorizontalPercentScrolled
properties.description: Returns or sets the horizontal scroll position as a percentage of the document width. Read/write Long.

properties.name: VerticalPercentScrolled
properties.description: Returns or sets the vertical scroll position as a percentage of the document length. Read/write Long.

properties.name: DocumentMap
properties.description: True if the document map is visible. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: Active
properties.description: True if the specified window is active. Read-only Boolean.

properties.name: Index
properties.description: Returns a Long that represents the position of an item in a collection. Read-only.

properties.name: IMEMode
properties.description: Returns or sets the default start-up mode for the Japanese Input Method Editor (IME). Read/write WdIMEMode.

properties.name: UsableWidth
properties.description: Returns the width (in points) of the active working area in the specified document window. Read-only Long.

properties.name: UsableHeight
properties.description: Returns the height (in points) of the active working area in the specified document window. Read-only Long. .

properties.name: EnvelopeVisible
properties.description: True if the email message header is visible in the document window. The default value is False. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: DisplayRightRuler

properties.name: DisplayLeftScrollBar

properties.name: Visible

properties.name: Thumbnails

properties.name: ShowSourceDocuments
properties.description: Returns or sets a WdShowSourceDocuments constant that represents how Microsoft Word displays source documents after a compare and merge process. Read/write.

methods.name: LargeScroll
methods.signature: LargeScroll([Down As Variant], [Up As Variant], [ToRight As Variant], [ToLeft As Variant])
methods.description: Scrolls a window or pane by the specified number of screens.

parameters.name: Down
parameters.description: The number of screens to scroll the window down.

parameters.name: Up
parameters.description: The number of screens to scroll the window up.

parameters.name: ToRight
parameters.description: The number of screens to scroll the window to the right.

parameters.name: ToLeft
parameters.description: The number of screens to scroll the window to the left.

methods.name: SmallScroll
methods.signature: SmallScroll([Down As Variant], [Up As Variant], [ToRight As Variant], [ToLeft As Variant])
methods.description: Scrolls a window or pane by the specified number of lines.

parameters.name: Down
parameters.description: The number of lines to scroll the window down. A "line" corresponds to the distance scrolled by clicking the down scroll arrow on the vertical scroll bar once.

parameters.name: Up
parameters.description: The number of lines to scroll the window up. A "line" corresponds to the distance scrolled by clicking the up scroll arrow on the vertical scroll bar once.

parameters.name: ToRight
parameters.description: The number of lines to scroll the window to the right. A "line" corresponds to the distance scrolled by clicking the right scroll arrow on the horizontal scroll bar once.

parameters.name: ToLeft
parameters.description: The number of lines to scroll the window to the left. A "line" corresponds to the distance scrolled by clicking the left scroll arrow on the horizontal scroll bar once.

methods.name: NewWindow
methods.description: Opens a new window with the same document as the specified window. Returns a Window object.

methods.name: PageScroll
methods.description: Scrolls through the specified pane or window page by page.

parameters.name: Down
parameters.description: The number of pages to be scrolled down. If this argument is omitted, this value is assumed to be 1.

parameters.name: Up
parameters.description: The number of pages to be scrolled up.

methods.name: SetFocus

methods.name: PrintOut
methods.signature: PrintOut([Background As Variant], [Append As Variant], [Range As Variant], [OutputFileName As Variant], [From As Variant], [To As Variant], [Item As Variant], [Copies As Variant], [Pages As Variant], [PageType As Variant], [PrintToFile As Variant], [Collate As Variant], [ActivePrinterMacGX As Variant], [ManualDuplexPrint As Variant], [PrintZoomColumn As Variant], [PrintZoomRow As Variant], [PrintZoomPaperWidth As Variant], [PrintZoomPaperHeight As Variant])
methods.description: Prints all or part of the document displayed in the specified window.

parameters.name: Background
parameters.description: Set to True to have the macro continue while Microsoft Word prints the document.

parameters.name: Append
parameters.description: Set to True to append the specified document to the file name specified by the OutputFileName argument. False to overwrite the contents of OutputFileName.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: The page range. Can be any WdPrintOutRange constant.

parameters.name: OutputFileName
parameters.description: If PrintToFile is True, this argument specifies the path and file name of the output file.

parameters.name: From
parameters.description: The starting page number when Range is set to wdPrintFromTo.

parameters.name: To
parameters.description: The ending page number when Range is set to wdPrintFromTo.

parameters.name: Item
parameters.description: The item to be printed. Can be any WdPrintOutItem constant.

parameters.name: Copies
parameters.description: The number of copies to be printed.

parameters.name: Pages
parameters.description: The page numbers and page ranges to be printed, separated by commas. For example, "2, 6-10" prints page 2 and pages 6 through 10.

parameters.name: PageType
parameters.description: The type of pages to be printed. Can be any WdPrintOutPages constant.

parameters.name: PrintToFile
parameters.description: True to send printer instructions to a file. Make sure to specify a file name with OutputFileName.

parameters.name: Collate
parameters.description: When printing multiple copies of a document, True to print all pages of the document before printing the next copy.

parameters.name: ActivePrinterMacGX
parameters.description: This argument is available only in Microsoft Office Macintosh Edition. For additional information about this argument, consult the language reference Help included with Microsoft Office Macintosh Edition.

parameters.name: ManualDuplexPrint
parameters.description: True to print a two-sided document on a printer without a duplex printing kit. If this argument is True, the PrintBackground and PrintReverse properties are ignored. Use the PrintOddPagesInAscendingOrder and PrintEvenPagesInAscendingOrder properties to control the output during manual duplex printing. This argument may not be available to you, depending on the language support (U.S. English, for example) that you have selected or installed.

parameters.name: PrintZoomColumn
parameters.description: The number of pages you want Word to fit horizontally on one page. Can be 1, 2, 3, or 4. Use with the PrintZoomRow argument to print multiple pages on a single sheet.

parameters.name: PrintZoomRow
parameters.description: The number of pages you want Word to fit vertically on one page. Can be 1, 2, or 4. Use with the PrintZoomColumn argument to print multiple pages on a single sheet.

types.remarks: Use the Windows property to return the Windows collection. The following example tiles all the windows so that they don't overlap one another. Use the Add method or the NewWindow method to add a new window to the Windows collection. Each of the following statements creates a new window for the document in the active window. The index number is the number to the left of the window name on the Window menu. The following example displays the caption of the first window in the Windows collection. A colon (:) and a number appear in the window caption when more than one window is open for a document. When you switch the view to print preview, a new window is created. types.name: Words
types.description: A collection of words in a selection, range, or document. Each item in the Words collection is a Range object that represents one word. There is no Word object.
types.remarks: Use the Words property to return the Words object. The following code example displays how many words are currently selected. Use Words (Index), where Index is the index number, to return a Range object that represents one word. The index number represents the position of the word in the Words collection. The following code example formats the first word in the selection as 24-point italic. The item in the Words collection includes both the word and the spaces after the word. To remove the trailing spaces, use the Visual Basic RTrim function - for example, RTrim(ActiveDocument.Words(1)). The following code example selects the first word (and its trailing spaces) in the active document. If the selection is the insertion point and it is immediately followed by a space, Selection.Words(1) refers to the word preceding the selection. If the selection is the insertion point and is immediately followed by a character, Selection.Words(1) refers to the word following the selection. types.name: XMLNamespace
types.description: Represents an individual schema within the Schema Library.
types.remarks: You can access the Schema Library from within Microsoft Word from the XML Schema tab in the Templates and Add-ins dialog box. The Schema Library represents schemas installed on a user's computer that a user has applied to a Word document or that a user has explicitly added to the Schema Library by using the Schema Library dialog box. Use the Item method of the XMLNamespaces collection to return an individual XMLNameSpace object. The index value of the Item method can be either a Long, which indicates the position of the schema in the Schema Library, or a String, which represents the name of the schema as returned using the URI property (the TargetNamespace setting defined in the schema). The following example attaches a schema named SimpleSample to the active document.

types.name: XMLNode
types.description: Represents a single XML element applied to a document.
types.remarks: Each XML element that has been applied to a document is displayed as a node in a tree view control in the XML Structure task pane. Each node in the tree view is an instance of an XMLNode object. The hierarchy in the tree view indicates whether a node contains child nodes. Use the Item method of the XMLNodes collection to return an individual XMLNode object. Use the Validate method to verify that an XML element is valid according to the applied schemas and that any required child elements exist and are in the required order. Once you run the Validate method, use the ValidationStatus property to verify whether an element is valid, and use the ValidationErrorText property to display information about what the user needs to do to make the document conform to the XML schema rules. The following example validates each of the XML elements in the active document. If the element is found to be invalid against the schema, the example returns a message to the user explaining what the problem is.

types.name: Zoom
types.description: Contains magnification options (for example, the zoom percentage) for a window or pane. The Zoom object is a member of the Zooms collection.
types.remarks: Use the Zoom property of the View object to return a single Zoom object. The following example sets the zoom percentage for the active window to 110 percent. Use Zooms (Index), where Index identifies the view type, to return a single Zoom object. The view type specified by index can be one of the following WdViewType constants: wdMasterView, wdNormalView, wdOutlineView, wdPrintPreview, wdPrintView, or wdWebView. The following example sets the magnification for the active window so that an entire page is visible. The Add method isn't available for the Zooms collection. The Zooms collection includes a single Zoom object for each of the various view types (such as outline, normal, or page layout).

You cannot enumerate the Zooms collection by using a For Each loop. Use Zooms (index), where index identifies the view type, to return a single Zoom object. The view type specified by index can be one of the following WdViewType constants: wdMasterView, wdNormalView, wdOutlineView, wdPrintPreview, wdPrintView, or wdWebView. The following example sets the magnification for the active window so that an entire page is visible. You can also use the Zoom property of the View object to return a single Zoom object. The following example sets the zoom percentage for the active window to 110 percent.
